excerpt: const { stdout, stderr, code } = await runProcess(`ffmpeg ${command}`, [], true);
sink: spawn(`ffmpeg ${command}`, [], {shell:true}) -- the whole string is executed as a shell command line
why: validatePath() only checks the path is non-empty (and, for inputs, exists on disk) -- it performs zero escaping. inputPath/watermarkPath/outputPath are interpolated unescaped inside double-quoted segments of the command string (`-i "${inputPath}" -i "${watermarkPath}" ... "${outputPath}"`), which is then passed whole as the 'command' argument to spawn() with shell:true and an empty args array -- meaning the entire string is handed to /bin/sh -c. A path containing a literal '"' followed by shell metacharacters breaks out of the quoted segment and injects arbitrary commands.
contract: Path where to save the watermarked video
